column8: Thu 19 Nov: 3c, and it corrects Q172-001: 'shall not, under any circumstances' was the template sentence of New South Wales works Acts since at least 1923 (a country railway), not a vow made for the Opera House, so the strength of a promise is in what pays it, not its words; fix Q172-001 (and its absorbed Q172-002) before use: never 'Parliament promised in law it would not' as a special vow, and 'rewritten three times', never 'amended four times' (row 17); absorbs row 2; as-made text read as a search-tool excerpt.

Thu 19 Nov: more instances of row 1's template (1927-1975, a 23,000-pound subway to an 11-million-pound dam); evidence for it, not a second idea; whether those works stayed inside their caps was not checked.
Thu 19 Nov: store: the ten per cent began in 1912 as a limit on a Minister's contracts with builders, then became a sentence about cost; background for row 1 only.
Thu 19 Nov: store: the cap was in the government's own bill and passed both Houses unamended; who wrote it does not explain why it failed, and the 1960 Hansard was not read.

Thu 19 Nov: the back-dated sanction (1 Jan 1957) and s 5's ratified contracts are more of Q172-003's order reversed (building first, law and money after); back-dating was routine, so it adds evidence, not a point.

Thu 19 Nov: store: the cap was a control device that made the building 'a political football' (Murray); quote only that phrase, since 'each 10 per cent increase' is Murray's gloss on one figure plus ten per cent.

Thu 19 Nov: store: the legal figure priced a roof whose geometry was solved only in 1961, so no percentage allowance could cover it; fix: the two Red Book figures conflict in Murray (4,781,200 and 4,812,000 pounds), so cite only the Act's 4,880,000 pounds; Q172-001 carries estimate-before-design.

Thu 19 Nov: store: the one early cap on the payer's own money (Cahill's 100,000 pounds) came before the law capped a cost; its outcome is UNVERIFIED and the State paid from 1976 (row 21), so never say it held.

Thu 19 Nov: the 1960 cap overtaken within about 18 months (5,368,000 pounds against 9.3 million in late 1961, Keel arithmetic checks) is one more re-estimate beside Q172-008, already absorbed by Q172-001.
Thu 19 Nov: store: the Premier's spoken 12.5 million pounds became the next legal figure; catalogue summaries, not the clippings.
Thu 19 Nov: store, the statute behind idea 1: the 1963 Act kept 'under any circumstances' through a 156% rise in its figure (12.5/4.88, Keel arithmetic checks); source for rows 1 and 12.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c candidate beside row 1: the Minister carrying the 1963 figure told the Assembly it could be exceeded while his Act kept 'under any circumstances', words with nothing behind them; fix: these are the City of Sydney catalogue's summaries, not Ryan's words, so read the SMH clippings or the Hansard of 6-7 Mar 1963 before quoting 'could exceed' or 'unreasonable'.

Thu 19 Nov: store, evidence for row 26: the 1963 cap plus ten per cent equalled the latest estimate, so its room was gone the day it passed (Keel arithmetic checks; the motive is inference); plan figures check (2.32% top, 3.16% bottom, NUMBERS 8u), but prose gives only the top's about 2%, in all, on today's figures.
Thu 19 Nov: store for row 15: a Minister unwilling to return to Parliament pushed the stated figure onto the designer (cut back to 12.5 million pounds); Q172-009 holds the control of payments.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b candidate, sharpens Q172-009 with figures: the lottery account held 5.15 million pounds and kept pace with costs when the 1965-66 crisis came, so the stated figure, not the cash, forced it; fix: never 'broke the project' or 'stopped it' (idea 3's title): the building was finished in 1973; say the crisis that ended Utzon's part came while the account was in credit; the account was a stream of ticket sales, not money owned; one Opera House fact per part.

Thu 19 Nov: store, 3a background: an Act's earmarked lottery surplus began paying the State's budget from 1965-66, so money tied to no dated payment can be claimed by other needs, while each Treasury is tied to a dated payment; pairs with Q62-008.

Thu 19 Nov: a wording correction to Q172-001 (absorbing Q172-002's 'amended in 1963, 1965, 1966 and 1969'): the 1965 touch was the Decimal Currency Act, so say the figure was rewritten three times (1963, 1966, 1969); the 25 million dollars is Keel arithmetic, never quoted.

Thu 19 Nov: source for row 24: in 1966 the cost words left the Act, leaving an authority to spend 'towards' the work up to 37.5 million dollars; a tranche, not a total, since the 1965 estimate was 49.4 million.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e store: when the money fight was lost the 1966 Act struck 'generally in accordance with' Utzon's design, so the building, not the figure, changed: one true example for Q5d-005's point that an overrun beyond the room falls on the building's size or design; the redesign had many causes.

Thu 19 Nov: source for row 24: the 1969 'maximum amount to be expended' equalled the latest estimate with no room above it; fix: drop 'even a cap on money fails': whether 102 million dollars passed the 85 million maximum is unresolved (scope, organ, car park), so never say the money cap failed (Q172-002's own rule).

Thu 19 Nov: the 1975 Act (spending from money provided by Parliament, the account swept into general revenue) is the statute behind Q172-019's payer whose money kept coming; Q172-004's critique already names s 4A.
Thu 19 Nov: store only: AMP's 1972 offer to build the car park at its own cost; why it did not go ahead is unknown, so never use it as a co-funder falling short (IPS l.15).

Thu 19 Nov: 3c: the standard history names 'the need to announce costs before they were known' among the overrun's causes, outside evidence for the spine (Q163-001: a promise breaks in the gap before its money exists); Laura's figure is a count of money owned, not a cost (Q172-001); Murray also blames the client committee and a hasty estimate, so never as the one cause.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, the corrected form of Q172-001's clause and the card's best: the Act's wording moved from an estimated cost that 'shall not ... be exceeded' (1960, 1963) to an authority 'towards' the work (1966) and 'the maximum amount to be expended' (1969), never to money already held, the step Laura takes (IPS l.15); fix: say the wording moved, never 'the law learned'; never that the 85 million maximum failed (row 20); one Opera House fact per part, so it replaces Q172-001 in 3c, never joins it; a government's spending limit, not a gift.
Thu 19 Nov: who paid the gap (ticket buyers, the State's budget, the architect, the design) is Q172-019's synthesis with Q172-009 and row 19's examples; whoever cannot walk away is Q172-018.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b, where the room sits: NSW's room for overruns sat inside the stated figure, while Laura's room for the building, her flexibility, sits outside every stated figure, with only a small room under each stated end for fund costs; figures check (2.32%, 3.16%, 24.9%, NUMBERS 8u); fix: in prose only the top's about 2% (in all, on today's figures), the bottom's 3.16% stays in the register; about 25% only 'if shares earn the 7.5% a year assumed'; never 'sized' (CANON A31); no slogan flip (room above a guess, below money); idea 3(b)'s 'about 2% under each stated figure' is wrong for the bottom.
Thu 19 Nov: the coercive deficiency is Q43-011's; the 1980 and 1905 quotations are new but read only through CRS R46417.
Thu 19 Nov: store: Dicey's sovereign that cannot bind itself is why 'under any circumstances' bound only Ministers; Laura's figure rests on money existing, not on her own rule holding.

Thu 19 Nov: store: s 7A held because it governed Parliament's own act and needed the voters to change it; its own break (Laura's rules are self-made) leaves only the parent's point, and the same-fortnight timing is decoration; 57.5% against 57.6% is rounding.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e: true (no building price sits in any promise's set in NUMBERS 8u; her flexibility cannot break a promise), but the register was built that way, so it predicts nothing new; 8u's own words carry it.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3, one clause beside the career line, and 3a: Savage's own test for a trustworthy small world fails for whoever holds tickets in the draw, and IPS l.9's writer holds them in shares; never as why the plan changed (CANON A3: the writer's income is the reason); the tie is a lag (Q148 row 14) against Savage's 'statistically independent'; co-sponsors 'can' cut in the same downturn, never 'together' (Q50); corrects Q168-023: Savage did give a working test in s5.5 (the lottery drum), so never 'Savage could give no criterion' or 'the plan answers what he left open' (fix Q168-023).
Thu 19 Nov: Savage's definition (a small-world consequence is a grand-world act) is the abstract form of row 3's Jones; row 3 carries where the plan's certainty stops.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e store: even a dollar prize is no sure consequence (Savage's Jones would buy a car if he feared inflation), and the case's nominal 50,000 dollars is what draws the line where the plan's certainty can reach; Q168-031 holds which holdings convert; never 'certain' for what the money buys (WORDS); absorbs rows 2 and 4.
Thu 19 Nov: a reason for WORDS's rule that 'certain' takes the Treasuries or the stated range as subject; a guard's reason, carried by row 3.

Thu 19 Nov: 3f check, store: a market-only model (a pseudo-microcosm) answers a question about markets, which is why the first plan's 96.8 in 100 was not the right test for a writer; fix: never say the 96.8 understated her risk (nothing measured that); IPS l.9's reason stays the reason (CANON A3) and Q168-007 holds the 96.8 against none.
Thu 19 Nov: store: Savage doubted his own test and found consolation only for constant prizes; his formula is garbled in the scan.

Thu 19 Nov: CONCEIT store: Savage's constant act (a result the same in every state) is a true fact behind the word ink, a payment met in every market state; never a technical term or a second image beside ink in prose; constant across market states only (an early fund end and fund costs at the edge, NUMBERS 3); read in the text layer, page not seen.
Thu 19 Nov: the payments need no forecast of markets is H7-016 (no forecast anywhere in what she promises); Savage's logic adds a name, not a point; across market states only.
Thu 19 Nov: Savage's typical small-world act is a lottery ticket, and Laura's purchase removes the draw: the same move as Q168-001 (Keynes's bond drawn by lot, her bonds take even the draw out).

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0: Savage gave both proverbs to one act (crossing a bridge when you reach it means confining attention to a world small enough to look before you leap), so each of the three dated steps (GOLDMINE 27) is a bridge reached and a small world built on it, and the top is fixed as late as the plan allows; corrects Q168-022 (and Q168 idea 3), which gave look to the payments and bridge to the building: fix Q168-022 before use; absorbs rows 11-12.
Thu 19 Nov: the price of looking is the same s2.5 passage as row 10; the 10.6% for a top stated 12 months early checks (NUMBERS 4: say the move would buy less than it, never 'not yet owned in').
Thu 19 Nov: Savage's timeless once-for-all decision is the foil for row 10's calendar of small worlds; never 'once for all' for the plan.
Thu 19 Nov: References only: cite Savage s2.5 p. 16 for the proverbs and s5.5 pp. 82-91 for small worlds, never s2.7.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3e, one clause: Binmore puts high finance in the large world, and the plan concedes it: each promise is kept safe by not depending on which surprise comes, not by foresight; absorbs rows 15 and 17; never 'invulnerable' for a stated end (row 16); one outside name per part.
Thu 19 Nov: Binmore's 'high finance most certainly' is row 14's large world in one line.

Thu 19 Nov: store: fix: never 'invulnerable to surprise' for a stated end (an early end of the late-2032 fund with cash at zero leaves the top up to 4,589 dollars short, NUMBERS 3), and the phrase is read only in Gintis's review; for the payments, row 14's wording.
Thu 19 Nov: Binmore's verdict that Savage's microcosms fail to shrink a large world is the background for row 14.
Thu 19 Nov: uncertainty aversion as a rational analogue of risk aversion defends the same step as row 26's Caution; one outside name per part.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the 7.5% is built from data (the row's own critique), so the mapping to a default from ignorance breaks; WORDS already makes every model result pencil.
Thu 19 Nov: no agreed method for probabilities is the problem row 23's two rationalities answer; co-sponsors can agree on a statement of holdings (Q168-030, Q22-020).
Thu 19 Nov: store; Dow and Werlang unread, and the plan trades at the move whatever the price, so a no-trade band fits IPS l.17 loosely; Bewley (the card's Gaps) is the better source.

Thu 19 Nov: store beside Q125-001 and card Q154: uncertainty about the odds favours the sure offer where promises to others are made (January 2027's price for the payments) and waiting where none is made yet (the top until the move); Nishimura and Ozaki unread.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, or a reason clause behind 3d: a promise to others must pass the convince-others test under every forecast, her flexibility only the cannot-be-shown-wrong test, so the plan's two pots follow the paper's two relations; absorbs rows 20 and 25; 3d's one outside parallel is the comfort letter, so never in Laura's words; one outside name per part.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, a concrete reason nothing is stated before the move: fifteen houses' forecasts point to two tops, while her flexibility, never stated, varies by house; figures check (NUMBERS 8p: thirteen of fifteen 115,000 dollars, GMO and Ninety One 110,000; half kept 12,998 to 22,699; NUMBERS 4: 95,000 to 140,000); fix: 'thirteen of fifteen' only with 8p's rule as it stands (Ninety One misses the step by 607 dollars), and the sameness after the move holds by construction, so say it as why the move comes first, never as a test passed; the mapping is Keel's.
Thu 19 Nov: convincing by sound argument, not style, is row 23's objective test in the authors' words; 3d's showable holding is Q22-020's.

Thu 19 Nov: 3f or 3a: Caution (choose the sure thing when reasons cannot settle it) is IPS l.11's step, applied to promised money only, and the authors' own 'rather extreme' is the cue to price the step once (aha row 10: about 1 in 31 against none); absorbs row 18; never as why the plan changed (CANON A3).
Thu 19 Nov: store for IPS l.17: a default (not guilty, the status quo) completes what reasons cannot settle, so the plan stays as written; evaluates the rule, adds none (CANON A34).

Thu 19 Nov: 3e frame beside Q109-003's reverse stress test: risk is an event that derails a reference narrative, so a fall in prices moves only pencil, and anything above the top is no risk; fix: map Kay's risk to NUMBERS 8u's ways a promise breaks, never to IPS l.17's two reasons (two lists, card Q109 row 33: never 'only two things can break the plan'); the book was not read.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e: Kay's modularity names the one weak module, the late-2032 fund (8w); fix: never 'about a quarter' (WORDS l.67; 8w: 'about 26%' of everything she holds on 1 Jan 2031, or 165,000 of the 615,000 dollars she owes or states), and the fund carries the top only from the move (from January 2028, the 2033 payment and the bottom); the same fix for idea 3(c).
Thu 19 Nov: store: Kay's reason for the house rule never to call the plan optimal; a guard's reason.
Thu 19 Nov: the signature quote (quibble over resemblance, never over identity) is the other half of row 2's correction.

Thu 19 Nov: store, the reason 2.0 says owned, never signed; corrects Q174-012, which read Lejeune as 'not a signature but an oath': the text says 'would not be I, the undersigned either', so a memoir is signed and sworn; fix Q174-012's wording before any use; absorbs row 1; never name a signature beside the definition (voice round 7).

Thu 19 Nov: store, the reason 'certain' takes the stated range without a probability label (Q71, Q74): on the day she speaks a stated end is held or not, while VT's value is argued by degrees; absorbs row 4; a sliver of degree stays (an early fund end at zero interest leaves the top up to 4,589 dollars short, NUMBERS 3), so never 'cannot move'.
Thu 19 Nov: 'all or nothing' is row 3's identity in five words; Lejeune softened it later (row 8).
Thu 19 Nov: store: a forecast is proved like a biography, by later resemblance; an owned figure starts from what is held; abstract.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, one clause, the sharper form of Q174-013: Lejeune's honest oath names its field and commits 'in any way' to nothing else, as Laura states the facility range and keeps her flexibility promised to no one (IPS l.15); Q174-013 should carry this half of p. 22, which is its rater's fix in Lejeune's words; one Lejeune row at most, never 'pact' in her words, never 'under-promise' or 'start low' (Q154); absorbs row 23.
Thu 19 Nov: credence rests on the figure being checkable, not checked: Q22-020's proof of funds from the custodian; funder reader 2 was simulated; never co-sponsors check Table 1's CUSIPs.
Thu 19 Nov: store: Lejeune's confession (a true statement exists once narrowed) argues the theory, not a plan decision.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d's store reason for leading with one figure: whoever receives an ambiguous message cannot sit between two chairs, and a range heard by funders is booked as one figure; fix: never offer the funder test as its check (four simulated readers, and each framing told them which figure to count, Q159-019, Q99-014); Lejeune means genre labels; row 6 holds the one Lejeune slot; absorbs rows 10 and 20.
Thu 19 Nov: autofictions read as memoirs is row 9's two chairs in practice; a stated figure is booked committed by a gift office (Q147).

Thu 19 Nov: store only: a rehearsal with four simulated readers, never evidence about funders (Q99-034); reader 3 booked 95,000 dollars with 20,000 'expected', so not four single figures; each framing named the figure to count (Q159-019), so it cannot check rows 9-10.
Thu 19 Nov: store: Lejeune's pact is a performative promise, and Laura's 2031 figure is a promise that is also a report of holdings; never that her words bind her in law (Q99 row 4).
Thu 19 Nov: a figure that binds only her yet orients co-sponsors is SD-1 (her figure is their target); her own 115,000 dollars first either way, the December 2032 condition the co-sponsors'.

Thu 19 Nov: store: Lejeune took 'fiduciaire' from finance; her figure asks trust in the Treasury, not in her (the trust moves, it is not removed); never 'fiduciary' in English prose, where it means a trustee's duty.
Thu 19 Nov: store: there is a frontier even where it is hard to draw, as VT is owned but pencil (Q157).

Thu 19 Nov: store or 3d background, the mirror image (a true book on the fiction shelf, a pencil figure filed as committed); fix: read Spiegelman's letter (NYT Book Review, 29 Dec 1991) before quoting 'queasy'.
Thu 19 Nov: store only: the book was not read, and a death camp's orchestra as a parallel for her money reads as glib in a finance report; 3d's flexibility clause needs no image; absorbs row 18.
Thu 19 Nov: Spiegelman's own gloss on row 17's panel; MetaMaus not read.
Thu 19 Nov: store; MetaMaus not read; the 7.5% stays in Table 2's note (above the middle of published forecasts).
Thu 19 Nov: the break (a funder's books cannot hold two versions) is row 9's point from the other side; the mapping is Keel's.
Thu 19 Nov: store; Chute read only as quoted in a review; never say her genre's rule is to state only what is held.
Thu 19 Nov: store: comics show their making, as 3c shows the rule's; 3c does that already.
Thu 19 Nov: Satrapi's 'only my truth' is row 6's field limit in a memoirist's practice; her side of the sum is SD-1's wording.
Thu 19 Nov: Bechdel's question at ten sets up row 25's circumflex; book not read.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, one clause at most: a hedge on every sentence hides the truth (Bechdel's circumflex), so the plan says fewer things and qualifies none; a parallel for a wording choice already made (3d's bare top), so F 2; fix: check Fun Home pp. 141-143 and 169 in the book before quoting; never in 3d or Laura's words.

Thu 19 Nov: store: the change it records (the margin named only in 3c, the top bare in 3d) is already in 3d's notes (funder test RESULTS); fix: two of four simulated readers, never 'the plan's own test caught' an effect.
Thu 19 Nov: store; Goya's plate not checked at source; 3d already names the warrant for the bottom (held since January 2028).
Thu 19 Nov: she states a 2033 figure in the past tense of a purchase is the spine (Q163-001: buys first, states after) in Lejeune's words; never 'cannot move' (NUMBERS 3).
Thu 19 Nov: store: Eakin's paraphrase restates 3d's rule of leaving out what would make a funder doubt the stated figure.
